\chapter{Communication Complexity — Rectangle}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.DeterministicCC.Rectangle
\section{Overview}

This module develops the combinatorial theory of \emph{rectangles} in the product
set $X \times Y$ as used in deterministic communication complexity.  It introduces
rectangles, monochromatic rectangles, fooling sets, and monochromatic rectangle
partitions, and proves the fundamental bound that the number of parts in any
monochromatic rectangle partition is at least the size of any fooling set.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Rectangle]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{pdf-d54d402b16e2-p007-b003}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}{pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p004-b006}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
\leanok
A subset $S \subseteq X \times Y$ is a \emph{rectangle} if it factors as a
product $A \times B$ for some $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Cross characterization of combinatorial rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle_iff}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{pdf-d54d402b16e2-p007-b003}
\proofsource{raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}{
  pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p004-b007,
  pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p004-b008,
  pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b001
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle_iff}
\leanok
\proofstep
  {CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
  {direct}
  {raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}
  {pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p004-b006}
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
\difficulty{4}
A subset $R \subseteq X \times Y$ is a rectangle — that is, $R = A \times B$ for some $A
\subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$ — if and only if it is closed under crossing: for all
$x, x' \in X$ and $y, y' \in Y$, whenever $(x, y) \in R$ and $(x', y') \in R$, both
mixed pairs $(x', y)$ and $(x, y')$ also lie in $R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Monochromatic set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonochromatic}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{pdf-d54d402b16e2-p008-b002}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}{pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b004}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonochromatic}
\leanok
A set $S \subseteq X \times Y$ is \emph{monochromatic} for a function
$g : X \to Y \to \alpha$ if $g$ is constant on $S$, i.e., $g\,x\,y = g\,x'\,y'$
for all $(x,y), (x',y') \in S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fooling set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsFoolingSet}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p009-b006,
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p010-b001
}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}{
  pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p011-b003,
  pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p011-b005
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsFoolingSet}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonochromatic, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
A set $S \subseteq X \times Y$ is a \emph{fooling set} for $g : X \to Y \to \alpha$
if every monochromatic rectangle with respect to $g$ contains at most one point
of $S$, i.e., $S \cap R$ is a subsingleton for every rectangle $R$ that is
monochromatic for $g$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Monochromatic rectangle partition]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-bootcamp}{
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p008-b004,
  pdf-d54d402b16e2-p008-b006
}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}{
  pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b003,
  pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b005
}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonochromatic, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
A collection $\mathcal{P}$ of subsets of $X \times Y$ is a \emph{monochromatic
rectangle partition} for $g : X \to Y \to \alpha$ if every member of
$\mathcal{P}$ is a rectangle, every member is monochromatic for $g$, the members
cover all of $X \times Y$, and distinct members are disjoint.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Every point lies in some part of a partition]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_point_mem}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_point_mem}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition}
\difficulty{2}
Let $g : X \times Y \to \alpha$ and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a monochromatic rectangle
partition for $g$. Then every point $p \in X \times Y$ belongs to at least one member $R
\in \mathcal{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of the part containing a point]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_part_unique}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_part_unique}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a monochromatic rectangle partition for a function $g : X \to Y \to
\alpha$, and let $R, S \in \mathcal{P}$. If some point $p \in X \times Y$ lies in both
$R$ and $S$, then $R = S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cross closure within a part]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_cross_mem}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_cross_mem}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a monochromatic rectangle partition for a function $g : X \to Y \to
\alpha$, and let $R \in \mathcal{P}$. If $(x,y)$ and $(x',y')$ both belong to $R$, then
the two "crossed" pairs $(x',y)$ and $(x,y')$ also belong to $R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Constant values within a part]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_values_eq}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_values_eq}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a monochromatic rectangle partition for a function $g : X \to Y \to
\alpha$, and let $R \in \mathcal{P}$. Then $g$ is constant on $R$: for any $(x,y),
(x',y') \in R$ we have $g\,x\,y = g\,x'\,y'$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.foolingSet_encard_le_of_monoPartition}
\proofsource{raoyehudayoff-ch01-deterministic-protocols}{pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p011-b005}

    pdf-fa052d8c95c0-p005-b003}
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsFoolingSet, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_point_mem}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be sets and let $g : X \times Y \to \alpha$. If $S \subseteq
X \times Y$ is a fooling set for $g$ and $\mathcal{P}$ is a monochromatic rectangle
partition for $g$, then the cardinality of $S$ is at most the cardinality of
$\mathcal{P}$, that is $\abs{S} \le \abs{\mathcal{P}}$, where cardinalities are compared
as extended natural numbers (allowing the value $\infty$).
\end{theorem}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsFoolingSet, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.foolingSet_encard_le_of_monoPartition}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g : X \times Y \to \alpha$, let $S \subseteq X \times Y$ be a fooling set for $g$,
and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a monochromatic rectangle partition for $g$. If $\mathcal{P}$
is finite, then the number of points of $S$ is at most the number of members of
$\mathcal{P}$; that is, $\abs{S} \le \abs{\mathcal{P}}$.
\end{theorem}
